Lef journal, issue 4

Alexander Rodchenko’s cover for the journal of the Left Front of the Arts splits its huge block-letter title into red and black halves.

Source
Art Institute of Chicago, 2009.485
Creator
Alexander Rodchenko (wrappers); Vladimir Mayakovsky (editor)
Made
1923–1924 (Art Institute of Chicago, for the set of seven issues)
Style
Constructivism (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Typographic, declarative, bold
Evidence
Viewed the Art Institute of Chicago image of the cover of issue 4 from its complete set, 2009.485 (843 × 1194 px), in a scratch folder. No image is stored. The issue number is read from the cover; the year of issue 4 (1924) is not stated on the museum record.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Art Institute of Chicago holds a complete set of the seven issues of Lef, 1923–24, with “2-color zincograph wrappers designed by Aleksandr Rodchenko” and contributions by Mayakovsky, Pasternak, Kruchenykh, Khlebnikov, Babel, Osip Brik, Tretyakov, and others. Art Institute of Chicago.

The same record lists illustrations by Rodchenko, Liubov Popova, Klutsis, Varvara Stepanova, and Anton Lavinskii. Art Institute of Chicago.

Observed

  • The lower half of the cover carries “ЛЕФ” in giant square block capitals. The top half of each letter is red and the bottom half is black, split on one horizontal line.
  • A thick vertical black bar runs down the left side of the upper half.
  • A poem in heavy black sans-serif lowercase steps down and to the right in short lines. The words “Лефа” and “вперед” are picked out in red.
  • “ДАЛЬШЕ!” is set in small red spaced capitals at the top left. A large red “4” sits at the top right.
  • The paper is a warm, slightly flecked tan. Red and black are the only inks.

Why it belongs

The cover has no diagonal. Its movement comes from the stepped poem and the split between red and black, which shows that the style’s energy can come from scale and color alone.

The block letters are built from rectangles, like the letters Lissitzky assembled from type material in Dlia golosa, published the same year.

Borrow

Set a short masthead in giant square capitals and split it horizontally into red and black.

Highlight the key words of a paragraph in red instead of bold or italic.
